name: Example DEX allow-list (pUSD, Portaldot V3 testnet)
policyName: Example DEX allow-list policy (pUSD, Portaldot V3 testnet, consumer v2)

binding.boundBy: allow-list operator (an AI agent on the author's machine); owner and reviewer are distinct accounts, both controlled by the ReviveCheck project

reviewerTrust: Only the ReviveCheck project's separate reviewer test account 0x95db300103ec8b45884b13ed85230fbf02114065 counts. The release owner 0x48b9e37a2a2c9621172745dc377b9fc6b9a6a71b and this reviewer are both controlled by the same project, so an approval shows on-chain role separation between two signers, not independent review. A production allow-list would name reviewers its operator does not control.

owner.control: the ReviveCheck project's development test account; it owns the pusd-catalog-v2 release and signed the listing

reviewer.control: the ReviveCheck project's separate reviewer test account; a distinct signer controlled by the same project, so this shows role separation, not independent review

operator.control: this repository's check command, run by an AI agent on the author's machine; it reads the chain and signs nothing

rule: An entry is allowed only when its binding evaluates to valid under this policy and the published fields equal the approved report field by field. A valid evaluation with a differing configured entry withholds the entry and names the field. The published fields come from the approved report, not from this configuration.
caveat: An allowed entry means the policy held at the recorded checkpoints and time; evaluate again before each use. The roles above say who controls each account. This allow-list establishes neither independent review nor adoption: both the release owner and the trusted reviewer are controlled by the ReviveCheck project.
